scope: The Aluvihare cave entrance and rock cleft at Matale as photographed in 1896, including the low tiled veranda, the rock-cut approach and steps, and the small upper shrine frontage in the cleft.
geometryBasis: Named OSM way 1197751507 outlines the narrow northwest-southeast temple cleft, between four specifically mapped bare-rock outcrops. Shared vertices and the Southeast entry from the road fix the approach and constrain the left veranda and inner stair.
sectionBasis: Cave’s eyewitness account places the tiled veranda on the left of the approach, with a cavern behind it. His photograph fixes the basic masonry, stair sequence and overhanging rock; component sizes, hidden backs and the alignment within the modern map are estimated.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Cave’s contemporary visit describes taking stone steps into the cleft and the long tiled veranda to his left over the entrance to the sacred cavern.
Original Woodburygravure, item RP-F-2001-7-285-3, titled ALUWIHARI, dated 1896, with named photographer and public-domain status.
Site description places the frontage terrace above a steep stone approach at the cave temple.
